newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Bank of Ireland's ICS pretax profit up 11pc.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Ireland's ICS pretax profit up 11pc.

text.p: Bank of Ireland Plc's ICS Building Society, said on Wednesday that it was well positioned to meet anticipated housing demand in Ireland in the years ahead.
The company, which reported a rise of 11 percent in pre-tax profit to 29.6 million Irish pounds, said 1996 was a very satisfactory year against a very competitive backdrop.

"ICS has set out to provide an extremely flexible range of competitively priced mortgage options for its customers and our innovative approach to product development has resulted in increased business," managing director Ted McGovern said in a results statement.

In summary, he said 1996 was a very satisfactory year for ICS and the society was now well positioned to play its part in meeting the anticipated demand for housing finance in Ireland in the years ahead.
In the context of recent concerns regarding house price inflation, McGovern said 99 percent of ICS advances were within standard criteria.
He reported a continued decline in arrears over the past four years including a 10 percent decline last year alone.

"In our view, the steep rise in house prices is due to market dynamics of supply and demand. With increasing national wealth and confidence, pent-up demand for housing is out-stripping supply. This demand is likely to increase significantly in the years ahead if the economy performs as forecast," McGovern said.
